Sure! To post a comment to **192.168.1.1** on VirusTotal V3 you’ll make a `POST` request to the `/ip_addresses/{ip_address}/comments` endpoint.  
Below is a quick‑start guide – pick whichever method feels most comfortable for you.

---

### 1️⃣ Quick‑Start Using *cURL*

```bash
curl --request POST \
     --url https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments \
     --header "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data @-
```

When prompted (`@-`) paste this JSON payload exactly as shown:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "type": "comments",
    "attributes": {
      "text": "Confirmed #malware"
    }
  }
}
```

Press **Enter**, then hit **Ctrl+D** (or your OS’s EOF) to finish sending the data.  

If everything goes well you’ll receive a `201 Created` status along with details of the newly created comment.

---

### 2️⃣ One‑liner (no file)

```bash
curl --request POST \
     --url https://www.virustable.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments \
     --header "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data "{\"data\":{\"type\":\"comments\",\"attributes\":{\"text\":\"Confirmed #malware\"}}}"
```

*(Make sure to escape quotes properly when running directly from a shell.)*

---

### 3️⃣ Python Snippet (requests library)

```python
import requests
import json

api_key = "ABC321"
ip_addr = "192.168.1.1"

payload = {
    "data": {
        "type": "comments",
        "attributes": {
            "text": "Confirmed #malware"
        }
    }
}

headers = {
    "x-apikey": api_key,
    "Accept": "application/vnd.api+json",
    "Content-type": "application/vnd.api+json"
}

resp = requests.post(
    f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{ip_addr}/comments",
    headers=headers,
    data=json.dumps(payload)
)

print(resp.status_code)
print(resp.json())
```

*Tip:* If you don’t already have `requests`, install it first:
```bash
pip install requests
```

---

#### What Happens Next?

Once the request succeeds, VirusTotal will return a JSON object describing the new comment, including its unique identifier (`id`). You can later retrieve or delete it using the same base URL but different endpoints (`GET` or `DELETE`).
